facts.text: Tariffville earned its name from the Tariff Act of 1824, which protected wool and cotton textiles and inspired the Tariff Manufacturing Company.
The Tariffville Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, preserves Greek Revival and Gothic Revival homes that date back to the 19th century.
Founded in 2003, the Tariffville Village Association works to protect the village’s natural resources and educate residents about its rich history.
Tariffville sits at the confluence of the Farmington River and Salmon Brook Wild and Scenic River, making it a hotspot for whitewater kayaking and national events.
The first steel manufacturing plant in the United States was built in Tariffville in 1727 along the Farmington River, marking an early industrial milestone.
The village’s Village Green and Gazebo serve as the focal point of its historic district and host community events that celebrate its four nationally recognized designations.
